items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A fixed public measurable path space of schedules on \([0,1]\), the structural and observed coordinates, and public class constants \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\) with \(0<p_{\min}\le1/2\) and \(0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\). The bounded model is \(\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), the causal target is \(\theta(P)=E_P[Y(a_0)]\), and \(\alpha\) is a public noncoverage level.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: Fixed \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), public \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), sample size \(n\), effective dimension \(d=2\beta+\kappa+1\), the three-regime localization scale and frontier \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\), minimax absolute risk, and minimum \(1-\alpha\) honest expected connected-interval length. The risk/length frontier uses \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\); finite honesty alone holds for \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The observable estimation layer takes public \(K\) as input. Its inverse-weight moments define \(b_q(K),B_q(K),V_q(K),A_q(K)\); empirical stratum ratios are clipped to \([0,1]\), the public dictionary selects \(\widehat q\), and \(C_{K,\alpha,n,\sigma}\) is the score-over-\(\alpha\) interval clipped to \([0,1]\), with \([0,1]\) as its small-sample fallback.

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The normalized filtered-Jacobi packet handle. A fixed smooth filter \(\eta\) is supported in \([9/8,15/8]\), and \(r=4\). For \(\kappa>0\) the endpoint Jacobi system \((r,(\kappa-1)/2)\) is used under \(z=2u^2-1\); for \(\kappa=0\) the interior symmetric system \((r,r)\) is centred at zero. Each gives the even, zero-extended packets \((\psi_m)_{m\ge4}\) supported on \([-1,1]\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl:
For public class constants \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\) satisfying \(0<p_{\min}\le1/2\) and \(0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\), fixed \(\beta,\kappa,\sigma\), and the public path space in \(\mathrm{def:potential\text{-}path\text{-}space\), let
\[
 \mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}
 =\left\{P:\begin{array}{l}
 \mathrm{ass:stratum\text{-}overlap},\ \mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}support},\
 \mathrm{ass:weak\text{-}design},\\
 \mathrm{ass:holder\text{-}mean},\ \mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}range},\
 \mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}channel},\\
 \mathrm{ass:error\text{-}independence},\
 \mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}unconfoundedness},\\
 \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes},\
 \mathrm{ass:consistency}\ \text{hold}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
Here \(P\) is a law of \((X,A,Z,Y(\cdot),Y)\), \(W=A+\sigma Z\), and the conditional means \(\mu_x\) are as in \(\mathrm{def:conditional\text{-}potential\text{-}mean\). The displayed assumptions alone carve the class. Binary outcomes, uniform ranks, rank--dose independence, and threshold schedules remain properties of the lower-bound subclass.

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: \(R_{K,n}(\sigma)=\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^n}|T-\theta(P)|\), where the infimum is over measurable, possibly randomized estimators.

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: \(H_{K,\alpha,n}(\sigma)=\inf_{C:\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}}Q_P^n\{\theta(P)\in C\}\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^n}[\operatorname{length}(C)]\), where \(C\) ranges over measurable connected intervals.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) contains \(q_h^{\mathrm F}\) over dyadic \(h\in[n^{-2},1/4]\), \(q_m^{\mathrm M}\) over odd \(m=2^j+1\le n^2\), and the constant weight; each weight is paired with its exact inverse \(\ell_h^{\mathrm F}\), \(\ell_m^{\mathrm M}\), or one, and is assigned the public score \(A_q\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: Given the public class constants \(K\), use the public modulo-three split \(\mathcal I_r=\{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:i\bmod3=r\}\). Compute the frequency, inverse-weight denominator and numerator estimates; project each empirical ratio to \([0,1]\) after flooring its denominator at \(b_q(K)/2\); combine strata into \(\widehat\theta_q\). Select the first minimizer \(\widehat q\) of the public score \(A_q(K)\) in the fixed dictionary order and return \(\widehat\theta=\widehat\theta_{\widehat q}\), with midpoint \(1/2\) when a split block is empty.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: Given public \(K\) and noncoverage level \(\alpha>0\), use the same blocks and selected dictionary representative as \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator\). For nonempty blocks set \(C_{K,\alpha,n,\sigma}=[\widehat\theta-A_{\widehat q}(K)/\alpha,\widehat\theta+A_{\widehat q}(K)/\alpha]\cap[0,1]\); otherwise return \([0,1]\).

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl:
Fix \(\eta(s)=\exp\{-1/((s-9/8)(15/8-s))\}\) for \(9/8<s<15/8\), and \(\eta(s)=0\) otherwise; this is the nonnegative smooth filter supported inside \((1,2)\) and positive on \([5/4,7/4]\) used throughout the proof. Let \(r=4\). Write \(\mathsf J_j^{(a,b)}\) for the standard Jacobi polynomial, and \(H_j^{a,b}\) for its squared norm under \((1-z)^a(1+z)^b\,dz\) on \([-1,1]\). For \(\kappa>0\), put \(b=(\kappa-1)/2\) and
\[
 K_m(z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(j/m)
   \frac{\mathsf J_j^{(r,b)}(-1)\mathsf J_j^{(r,b)}(z)}{H_j^{r,b}},
 \qquad
 \psi_m(u)=\mathbf1\{|u|\le1\}(1-u^2)^r
             \frac{K_m(2u^2-1)}{K_m(-1)}.
\]
For \(\kappa=0\), use the interior symmetric construction
\[
 \widetilde K_m(u)=\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(j/m)
   \frac{\mathsf J_j^{(r,r)}(0)\mathsf J_j^{(r,r)}(u)}{H_j^{r,r}},
 \qquad
 \psi_m(u)=\mathbf1\{|u|\le1\}(1-u^2)^r
             \frac{\widetilde K_m(u)}{\widetilde K_m(0)}.
\]
These formulas name the filtered-Jacobi handle for integers \(m\ge4\); values outside \([-1,1]\) are zero. Positivity of the normalizing denominators, weighted moment cancellation, localization, and derivative bounds are established in \(\mathrm{thm:weighted\text{-}packet\text{-}construction}\), rather than asserted as properties of this definition.

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl:
Fix a public measurable path space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) of Borel functions from \([0,1]\) to \(\mathbb R\), with jointly measurable evaluation
\[
 e:\mathcal S\times[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathbb R,
 \qquad e(f,a)=f(a).
\]
Schedules are extensional: \(f=g\) if and only if \(e(f,a)=e(g,a)\) for every \(a\in[0,1]\). The domain carries \(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal B([0,1])\). The space is taken to include the threshold schedules through the measurable map
\[
 \iota:C([0,1],[0,1])\times[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathcal S,
 \qquad \iota(f,u)(a)=\mathbf1\{u\le f(a)\},
\]
where \(C([0,1],[0,1])\) has its uniform-norm Borel sigma algebra. The results are stated for every such fixed public path space; no continuity or monotonicity of a general member path is required. The potential-outcome schedule \(Y(\cdot)\) is a measurable random element of \(\mathcal S\), and \(Y(a)=e(Y(\cdot),a)\).

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl:
For a law \(P\), each \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(p_x>0\), and each \(a\in[0,1]\), define
\[
 \mu_x(a)=E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]
 =\frac{E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}Y(a)]}{p_x}.
\]
The expectation exists and belongs to \([0,1]\) under \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes}\). This definition names the conditional potential-outcome mean; it does not assume any identity involving the realized treatment. In the model class, \(\mathrm{ass:stratum\text{-}overlap}\) supplies \(p_x>0\) for both strata.

items.label: Assumption A-1
items.nl: For a public constant \(p_{\min}\in(0,1/2]\), \(p_{\min}\le p_x\le1-p_{\min}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

items.label: Assumption A-3
items.nl: For public constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\), every \(g_x\) is a Lebesgue density satisfying \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}|t|^{\kappa}\le g_x(t)\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}|t|^{\kappa}\) for almost every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\).

items.label: Assumption A-4
items.nl: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the radius-one Holder condition \(\mu_x\in\mathcal H^{\beta}([0,1])\) means exactly \(|\mu_x(a)-\mu_x(a')|\le|a-a'|^\beta\) for all \(a,a'\in[0,1]\), with no supremum-norm term; the unit-interval range is imposed separately.

items.label: Assumption A-10
items.nl: With \(P\)-probability one, the random schedule satisfies \(Y(a)=\mathbf 1\{U\le\mu_X(a)\}\) simultaneously for every \(a\in[0,1]\).

items.label: Assumption A-12
items.nl: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).

items.label: Assumption A-13
items.nl: \(Y(\cdot)\perp A\mid X\), as conditional independence of the measurable random schedule and the dose.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: Fix public \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\). For every admissible nonnegative weight \(q\) and exact Gaussian inverse \(\ell_q\), the localized ratio \(m_{x,q}\) is well defined and obeys \(E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)]\ge p_{\min}c_{\mathrm{lo}}I_\kappa(q)\) and \(|m_{x,q}-\mu_x(a_0)|\le(c_{\mathrm{hi}}/c_{\mathrm{lo}})I_{\kappa+\beta}(q)/I_\kappa(q)\), uniformly including \(\sigma=0\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
Let \(\Phi_\sigma\) denote the centered Gaussian probability measure with variance \(\sigma^2\), with \(\Phi_0=\delta_0\).  If \(
u_1\) and \(
u_2\) are finite signed Borel measures supported on \([-1/2,1/2]\) and \(
u_1*\Phi_\sigma=
u_2*\Phi_\sigma\), then \(
u_1=
u_2\) for every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl: For public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), the schedule-level assumptions imply \(E_P[Y\mid A,X,Z]=\mu_X(A)\) almost surely. In particular \(0\le Y\le1\) almost surely and \(E_P[Y\mid A,X]=\mu_X(A)\) almost surely.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
For real \(a,b>-1/2\), integer \(j\ge0\), and real \(z\), the standard Jacobi polynomial has the representation
\[
 P_j^{(a,b)}(z)
 =2^{-j}\sum_{i=0}^{j}
 \binom{j+a}{i}\binom{j+b}{j-i}
 (z-1)^{j-i}(z+1)^i.
\]
Here \(\binom{v}{i}=v(v-1)\cdots(v-i+1)/i!\), with
\(\binom{v}{0}=1\), is the generalized binomial coefficient; all notation is local to this identity.

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl: For public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), \(n\ge3\), \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), every member law, and every admissible inverse pair with finite public second moment, the split estimator clipped to \([0,1]\) satisfies the public expected-error certificate \(E|\widehat\theta_q-\theta(P)|\le A_q(K)\). It remains defined if either stratum is absent from a split block.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl: Fix public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), and \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). Every pair in \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) is admissible with finite public inverse-weight second moment. There are \(C>0\) and \(n_0\), depending on \(K,\beta,\kappa\) but not on \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), such that the selected score satisfies \(A_{\widehat q}(K)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}\) for \(n\ge n_0\), with Fourier witnesses in the first two regimes and polynomial inverse-heat witnesses in the third.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: Fix public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\). For any two laws in \(\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) with the same observed law, Gaussian deconvolution identifies each stratum mass, latent dose measure, and latent mean measure; local positive-mass ratios and Holder continuity identify every \(\mu_x(a)\), including \(a_0\). Hence \(\theta(P)=\sum_xp_x\mu_x(a_0)\) is identified, including at \(\sigma=0\).

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
For every fixed \(\kappa\in[0,2]\) there are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(c>0\), and an explicit sequence of even, continuously differentiable zero-extended functions \((\psi_m)_{m\ge4}\) supported on \([-1,1]\), obtained from the filtered-Jacobi handle, such that
\[
 \psi_m(0)=1,\qquad \|\psi_m\|_\infty\le C,\qquad
 \|\psi_m'\|_\infty\le Cm,
\]
\[
 \int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa|\psi_m(u)|\,du\le Cm^{-\kappa-1},\qquad
 \int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa\psi_m(u)^2\,du\le Cm^{-\kappa-1},
\]
and
\[
 \int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa u^j\psi_m(u)\,du=0
 \quad\text{for every integer }0\le j<cm.
\]
For \(\kappa=0\) the construction is centered at the interior point zero in a symmetric Jacobi system and does not use an endpoint limit.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: For every public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), and \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), there are \(C>0\) and \(n_0\), depending on \(K,\beta,\kappa\), such that the public estimator \(\widehat\theta_K\) has expected absolute error at most \(C\rho_{n,\sigma}\) for every \(n\ge n_0\), \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\). The dictionary includes the stated Fourier and polynomial comparison witnesses.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl: For every public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the interval \(C_{K,\alpha,n,\sigma}\) covers \(\theta(P)\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) for every sample size, \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\). Its worst-law expected length is at most \(C(K,\beta,\kappa,\alpha)\rho_{n,\sigma}\) uniformly in \(\sigma\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl: Fix public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and any total-variation level \(\tau>0\). If \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le(\kappa+1)2^\kappa\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\), then for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), explicit Bernoulli threshold laws in \(\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) share the same latent design, have target separation at least \(c(K,\beta,\kappa,\tau)\rho_{n,\sigma}\), and have product observed-law total variation at most \(\tau\).

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl: Fix public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\). If \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le(\kappa+1)2^\kappa\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\), then minimax absolute risk and minimum \(1-\alpha\) honest expected connected-interval length over \(\mathcal P_{K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) are both of order \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\), uniformly over \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\). The two transition windows and the fixed-positive-noise order remain as stated, with constants depending on \(K,\beta,\kappa,\alpha\).

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl: Fix public \(K\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), with \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le(\kappa+1)2^\kappa\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\). At \(\sigma=0\), minimax risk and minimum \(1-\alpha\) honest expected connected-interval length over the same class are both of order \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\); the separate Gaiffas direct benchmark has the same pointwise weak-design order.

items.label: Cited result lem:filtered-jacobi-localization
items.nl:
Let \(a,b>-1/2\), let \(\eta\in C^\infty[0,\infty)\) have support in \([1/2,2]\), and let
\[
 K_m^{a,b}(x,y)=\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(j/m)\frac{P_j^{(a,b)}(x)P_j^{(a,b)}(y)}{H_j^{a,b}}.
\]
Writing \(d(x,y)=|\arccos x-\arccos y|\) and
\[
 W_{a,b}(m;x)=(1-x+m^{-2})^{a+1/2}(1+x+m^{-2})^{b+1/2},
\]
for every \(S>0\) there is \(C_S<\infty\) such that
\[
 |K_m^{a,b}(x,y)|\le
 \frac{C_Sm}{\sqrt{W_{a,b}(m;x)W_{a,b}(m;y)}(1+md(x,y))^S}
\]
for all \(m\ge1\) and \(x,y\in[-1,1]\).

items.label: Cited result lem:filtered-jacobi-lipschitz
items.nl:
Let \(a,b>-1/2\), let \(\eta\in C^\infty[0,\infty)\) have support in \([1/2,2]\), and define
\[
 K_m^{a,b}(x,y)=\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(j/m)\frac{P_j^{(a,b)}(x)P_j^{(a,b)}(y)}{H_j^{a,b}},
 \quad d(x,y)=|\arccos x-\arccos y|,
\]
\[
 W_{a,b}(m;x)=(1-x+m^{-2})^{a+1/2}(1+x+m^{-2})^{b+1/2}.
\]
For every \(S>0\) and fixed \(c_*>0\) there is \(C<\infty\) such that, whenever \(d(x,\xi)\le c_*/m\) and \(d(z,\xi)\le c_*/m\),
\[
 |K_m^{a,b}(x,y)-K_m^{a,b}(\xi,y)|
 \le
 \frac{Cm^2d(x,\xi)}{\sqrt{W_{a,b}(m;y)W_{a,b}(m;z)}(1+md(y,z))^S}.
\]

items.label: Cited result lem:jacobi-norm
items.nl:
For real \(a,b>-1/2\), the standard Jacobi polynomials \(P_j^{(a,b)}\), \(j=0,1,\ldots\), are orthogonal for the weight
\(w_{a,b}(z)=(1-z)^a(1+z)^b\) on \([-1,1]\). In particular
\[
 \int_{-1}^{1}w_{a,b}(z)P_j^{(a,b)}(z)R(z)\,dz=0
 \quad\text{for every polynomial \(R\) of degree less than \(j\)}.
\]
Their positive squared norms are
\[
 H_j^{a,b}:=\int_{-1}^{1}w_{a,b}(z)P_j^{(a,b)}(z)^2\,dz
 =\frac{2^{a+b+1}}{2j+a+b+1}
 \frac{\Gamma(j+a+1)\Gamma(j+b+1)}
 {\Gamma(j+1)\Gamma(j+a+b+1)}.
\]
All parameters in this statement are local Jacobi notation.

items.label: Cited result lem:gamma-ratio
items.nl:
For fixed real shifts \(s,t\), as the positive real number \(z\) tends to infinity with \(z+s>0\) and \(z+t>0\),
\[
 \frac{\Gamma(z+s)}{\Gamma(z+t)}\sim z^{s-t}.
\]
Here \(\sim\) means that the ratio of the two sides tends to one, and the parameters are local to this statement.

items.label: Cited result lem:gaiffas-direct-benchmark
items.nl:
Consider Gaiffas's direct regression observations
\(B_i=f(D_i)+\xi_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with \(D_i\in[0,1]\), independent identical draws,
\(\xi_i\sim N(0,\tau_{\mathrm G}^2)\) independent of the design. Fix
\(x_*\in(0,1)\), \(0<s\le1\), \(0\le v\le2\), and
\(c,r,M,\tau_{\mathrm G}>0\). The fixed design density is
\(c|u-x_*|^v\) near \(x_*\). Put \(\omega(a)=ra^s\) and
\[
 h_{\mathrm G,n}
 =\left\{\frac{\tau_{\mathrm G}^2(v+1)}{2cr^2n}\right\}^{1/(2s+v+1)}.
\]
Let \(\mathscr P_k\) be the real polynomials of degree at most \(k\).
Definition 2's specialized class is
\[
 \Sigma_n=\left\{f:\|f\|_\infty\le M,\quad
   \inf_{p\in\mathscr P_{\lfloor s\rfloor}}
   \sup_{|u-x_*|\le a}|f(u)-p(u-x_*)|\le\omega(a)
   \text{ for every }0<a\le h_{\mathrm G,n}\right\},
\]
with Borel \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\). For sufficiently large \(n\), the
neighborhoods are inside the design's power-law region. Theorem 1, with
loss parameter one, gives
\[
 \inf_{\widehat f}\sup_{f\in\Sigma_n}
 E_f|\widehat f(x_*)-f(x_*)|
 \asymp\omega(h_{\mathrm G,n})
 \asymp n^{-s/(2s+v+1)}.
\]
The infimum is over measurable estimators from these observations; \(E_f\) denotes their observed-law expectation. All constants here are fixed. The class retains \(\mathscr P_1\) at
\(s=1\). This is a direct Gaussian-response benchmark, without any claim
of inclusion of the present causal class or any honest-length guarantee.
